The CBS12 News I-Team has been closely following Port St. Lucie's election cycle, as there are two headline stories playing out and the future of the city is at stake. Leadership and trash are the hot-button items. On the first day of early voting in St. Lucie County, our crew visited a polling location on Rosser Blvd. We found two tents, side by side. In them, two candidates for mayor-- with such a rift between them-- the race feels like a war. The incumbent, Shannon Martin, is running to stay in office, and she says the city needs to stay on its current course. She points to how she has prioritized infrastructure repairs, like roadwork, as a reason to keep her in City Hall. Her opponent, Steven Giordano, says City Hall is corrupt and has lost touch with everyday people. When pressed on specific things he’d do differently-- he also wanted to talk about roadwork and says the city needs a new traffic study. See also: Martin County airport committee to review overnight flights and noise concerns Mayors serve four-year terms and wield significant influence in the mayor-council form of government. But trash collection is another issue getting people fired up: Should the city switch to twice-a-week pickup? FCC is the company that handles garbage collection in Port St. "I don't want to pay for something I don't need," said resident Rob Buske. Buske is making a point we have seldom heard while covering trash in the city. At many recent city council meetings, members of the public have hurled angry comments at city leaders, saying the trash pickup is sub-par. They’ve demanded an additional collection day. Ironic, then, that on the first day of early voting, everyone we asked for comment said they’d rather keep what they’ve got. The ballot question about trash collection isn't binding; it’s simply a way to poll the residents. The council might or might not go with whatever the majority of voters say. A second pick-up day would cost residents more than a hundred bucks a year, but some are adamant it's necessary. As this story comes to air and online, the election is less than 2 weeks away. Candidates for Mayor do not declare a party, and trash is a non-party matter. Here it's not Republicans vs. Democrats, but it’s somehow more personal, more granular, while also being big-picture. When can my garbage go to the curb? Who will be in charge of the city and what's their vision? The people are about to decide.

A water storage tank in Fort Pierce was named the winner of the 2026 Tank of the Year. The annual contest held by Tnemec Company, Inc., a leading provider of high-performance coatings, announced the winner and Top 12 finalists on Friday. "Pretty excited," said Christian Stanley of C. Stanley Creative, the artist behind the tank. "I got the call earlier from our sales rep. He was excited to share that we were the first-place winner of Tnemec's Tank of the Year. And yeah, we're just beyond excited, and I'm excited to share that with them and with the community that they have an award-winning piece of public art there in their community." Located in Jaycee Park, the winning ground storage tank showcases a vibrant mural celebrating Florida's coastal environment and native wildlife. The mural features sea turtles, dolphins, manatees, pelicans, and tropical fish, transforming essential water infrastructure into a community landmark. The tank is protected with Tnemec's Series 1026 Enduratone coating. According to Tnemec Company, Inc., a panel of water tank enthusiasts selected the Fort Pierce tank based on its artistic value, significance to the community, and challenges encountered during the project. "For 20 years, this competition has showcased how communities can transform essential infrastructure into something truly special," said Kevin Morris, director of sales for the water tank market at Tnemec. "The creativity and community pride reflected in this year's entries are remarkable. Fort Pierce is a great example of how a water tank can become more than a functional structure. It can become a landmark that residents are proud to call their own." Digital content reporter Camila Pereira visited the tank last week as Stanley and his wife Jessica traveled from Central Florida for a couple of days to apply that UV clear coat. Stanley shared their excitement of it being in the running, and the honor they felt of being selected by Fort Pierce Utilities Authority to leave their mark where he grew up. On Friday, WPBF 25 News reconnected with Stanley and shared how he felt about the win. "We were runners-up in 2024, and that was exciting," he said. "But I was like, man, I really want to try. And I know we can make something that would win the first-place award. So, it's, you know, taken a couple of years for us to get there. But I'm excited that we were able to come some bring something together and that Fort Pierce trusted us to make something that we felt was going to be really impactful and iconic for the community there." Fort Pierce Utilities Authority shared the following statement with WPBF 25 News: "We are thrilled and deeply grateful to receive the Tank of the Year award. Thank you to everyone who voted and supported us, and to the teams who made it happen. It has been an absolute pleasure and honor for our team here at FPUA to collaborate with the artist and the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency this summer, turning the Jaycee Park Water Tank into a Fort Pierce landmark. Rachel Tennant, FPUA Director of Public Affairs Sustainability Stanley said it's an honor to be recognized nationally, but an even bigger honor to have his work displayed at home for the community to enjoy. "I grew up in Stuart, so it was great to visit kind of my old hometown and just be back in the community and be a part of it again, and to kind of leave a footprint," he said. "This thing will kind of continue to have a life of its own beyond just the just the tank. And it'll have a bigger footprint than even what we could anticipate. So, it's really cool to get some recognition for the for the award. And we're excited to see what comes next from this." The Fort Pierce tank will be featured as January in Tnemec's 2027 water tank calendar, with the remaining finalists and nominees featured throughout the calendar. The 2026 Tank of the Year winner and Top 12 finalists are: Tank of the Year: Fort Pierce, Florida People's Choice: Detroit Lakes, Minnesota Oak Harbor, Washington Percival, Iowa South Haven, Michigan Shreveport, Louisiana Prior Lake, Minnesota Scranton, South Carolina Elloree, South Carolina Cheyenne, Wyoming Pelham, Alabama Walnut Cove, North Carolina

Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause after months of controversy, hazing allegations, and a no-confidence vote. Interim Chief Paul Langel said, "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process." The decision comes two months after five firefighters were displaced for allegedly turning a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and using it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs. One of the terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson, said, "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don’t think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department." The disciplined firefighters have called the termination retaliation for previous complaints they filed against district leadership. When asked about the possibility of the terminated firefighters regaining their jobs, Langel said, "I believe that there’s always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I’ve got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics." The board voted to appoint Langel as interim chief. He is a familiar face in the district, with 30 years of experience. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early. A 22-year-old man from New York is facing charges in an organized check fraud and money laundering scheme, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office Economic Crimes Unit conducted a multi-jurisdictional investigation, culminating in the arrest of Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx. A check mailed by a Port St. Lucie real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered, and deposited into a bank account established using a stolen identity, the sheriff's office said. Detectives traced the stolen funds through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers allegedly used to conceal their origin before the money was deposited into Diallo’s personal bank account. Detectives obtained an arrest warrant charging Diallo with money laundering ($300–$20,000), scheme to defraud ($50,000 or more) and grand theft. 14, Diallo was apprehended by Canadian border authorities while attempting to enter Canada from the United States. He was detained at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Total bond was set at $30,000 for the three charges. “Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice,” Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable.” Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

An 86-year-old man was found dead inside a car submerged in the Indian River Lagoon in Vero Beach after witnesses said the vehicle drove through a fence and into the water. The incident occurred at a condo complex, where residents said they knew the driver. Police have not yet identified the man. Tire marks were visible near the scene, and the silver Honda CRV was pulled from the water as police worked for hours to investigate. Authorities said the man had gone missing the night before. Residents on Greytwig Road were later seen cleaning up the parking lot, removing mud and scrubbing away tire marks. Many described the scene as unsettling. The investigation remains active as police work to determine what led up to the crash.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Mourns Second Hodge Brother in a Year
hero.body:
A firefighter-paramedic with the St. Lucie County Fire District died Saturday morning while on duty, just over a year after his brother, also a member of the department, died in similar circumstances. Austin Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce.

Austin's brother, Jarius Hodge, died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. On May 30, friends and family gathered for a cookout and balloon release to celebrate what would have been Jarius's 27th birthday. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today."

On Saturday, a procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted Austin Hodge from the hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Fire District, which operates 20 fire stations with 523 firefighters, said in a statement that his death "is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community" and extended "heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." The district said information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized.

The department also thanked agencies across the region for their support in the hours after the loss. In a Facebook post, the district wrote, "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another. Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin's family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Condolences also came from Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. The district also lost firefighter Connor Whitehead, 21, who died on May 31.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies On Duty A Year After Brother's Death
cards.teaser: Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, 15 months after his younger brother Jarius died following treatment at Cleveland Clinic Tradition in Port St. Lucie. Austin had publicly pushed for accountability over his brother's death and criticized Florida's medical malpractice laws.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, more than a year after his younger brother Jarius, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died at age 26. The St. Lucie County Fire District announced Hodge's line-of-duty death on Oct. 24, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, served the community for more than nine years, and was assigned to Station 9. The circumstances surrounding his death have not been released.

Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue shared condolences following Hodge's unexpected death Saturday morning. The St. Lucie County Fire District asked the public to respect Hodge's family as they grieve and said additional information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor his service will be shared in coordination with the family once finalized.

Hodge's death comes more than a year after his brother Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

In that earlier interview, Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025 and went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22 struggling to breathe, but died hours later. Austin alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating his brother, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said Jarius had been healthy before becoming ill. Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for Jarius' death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," Austin said. He emphasized that his family sought accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable."

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Man in Oct. 9 Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured Jogger
hero.teaser: Detectives used surveillance video and the victim's Garmin watch data to identify a suspect in the hit-and-run that left a 63-year-old man with severe head injuries. Eric Saint Aude, 60, has been arrested on a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a man in connection with an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old jogger critically injured. Eric Saint Aude, 60, was taken into custody and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

The crash happened around 12:56 a.m. near NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. Officers found the 63-year-old man unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital and remains in critical condition.

Investigators identified the victim using information from his Garmin watch, which they traced back to his home. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said night-shift officers were familiar with the victim from his regular exercise routine. "Our officers that work night we're used to seeing him out exercising in the evening and he was known to jog, walk in the street medians," Niemczyk said.

Detectives reviewed surveillance video along with additional evidence to identify Saint Aude as a suspect in the crash. That investigative work led to his arrest on the hit-and-run charge, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

hero.headline: FHP Report: Freightliner Turned Into SUV's Path in Fatal Indian River Crash
hero.body:
A newly released Florida Highway Patrol report details how a 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday when the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. The traffic homicide investigation remains open, and the man's next of kin had not been notified as of the report.

According to the crash report, a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was stopped at a stop sign on westbound 49th Street and attempted to turn left when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner did not report any injuries.

Florida Highway Patrol's traffic homicide investigation into the crash is ongoing.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, a Year After Brother's Death
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter/paramedic Austin Hodge died Saturday morning while on duty, the district confirmed. His death comes just over a year after his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, also a district firefighter, died in the line of service.

Austin Hodge joined the St. Lucie County Fire District on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies left the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning to mark his death.

Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. People gathered on May 30 to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. At the time, Austin Hodge said of his brother, "He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today."

Austin Hodge's death marks the third loss for the department in recent months. Firefighter Connor Whitehead, 21, died on May 31. The St. Lucie County Fire District operates 20 fire stations and employs 523 firefighters, according to the agency. "His death is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," the district said in a statement. "The District extends its heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." Several agencies offered condolences, including Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, the Indian River County Emergency Services Department and Indian River County Fire Rescue.

hero.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud, Money Laundering Case
hero.teaser: Detectives traced a stolen, altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers before linking it to a 22-year-old New York man.
hero.body:
A 22-year-old man from the Bronx has been extradited to St. Lucie County to face charges after detectives linked him to a check stolen from a Port St. Lucie real estate company and funneled through a money laundering scheme, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday. Gibrill Diallo faces charges of money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more, and grand theft.

The Sheriff's Office Economic Crimes Unit launched a multi-jurisdictional investigation after a check mailed by the Port St. Lucie real estate company was stolen and fraudulently altered. The check was deposited into a bank account opened using a stolen identity, according to the Sheriff's Office. Detectives then traced the money as it moved through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers, which investigators say were used to disguise where the funds originated, before the money landed in Diallo's personal bank account.

Diallo was apprehended on Oct. 14 by Canadian border authorities as he attempted to enter Canada from the United States. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Bond was set at a total of $30,000 across the three charges.

"Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice," St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable."

cards.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee in 4-3 Vote
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against his leadership. The board appointed Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief following the decision.

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced for allegedly turning a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and using it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident. The disciplined firefighters have called their termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

Langel said he sees his new role as a chance to move the department forward. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics," he said.

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the firefighters terminated in the hazing case, said he welcomed the board's decision to remove Lee. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," he said. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early. The question of whether the three fired firefighters could be reinstated remains unresolved as Langel settles into his new role.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Mayor's Race, Trash Pickup Question Top Nov. Ballot
hero.body:
Early voting is underway in Port St. Lucie, where voters will decide a tense mayoral race between incumbent Shannon Martin and challenger Steven Giordano, along with a non-binding ballot question asking whether the city should switch to twice-a-week trash pickup, a change that would cost residents more than $100 a year. Election day is less than two weeks away.

On the first day of early voting, campaign tents for Martin and Giordano stood side by side outside a polling location on Rosser Boulevard, reflecting what has become a bitter contest. Martin is running for another term and argues the city should stay on its current course, pointing to infrastructure work, including roadwork, as evidence her administration is delivering results. Giordano has accused City Hall of corruption and of losing touch with everyday residents. When asked what he would do differently, he also pointed to roadwork, saying the city needs a new traffic study. Port St. Lucie's mayor serves a four-year term and holds significant power under the city's mayor-council form of government. Neither candidate is running with a party affiliation, since the mayoral race is nonpartisan.

The ballot also asks voters whether the city should add a second weekly trash collection day. FCC handles garbage collection in Port St. Lucie. The question will not bind the city council, which could choose to ignore the outcome regardless of how residents vote. At recent city council meetings, residents have complained that current trash service is inadequate and have pushed for an additional pickup day. Resident Rob Buske offered a different view, saying, "I don't want to pay for something I don't need." On the first day of early voting, people asked about the issue said they would rather keep the current one-day pickup schedule, even as others have demanded a change.

The trash question, like the mayoral race, is nonpartisan, but both issues have generated strong feelings among residents. The choice over who leads the city comes down to differing visions for Port St. Lucie's direction, while the trash question centers on a simpler, more immediate concern: how often garbage gets picked up at the curb. Both items will appear on the same ballot as voters decide the city's near-term direction over the next two weeks.

hero.headline: PSL Police Arrest Man in Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured 63-Year-Old on NW California Blvd
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a man they say struck a 63-year-old resident with his vehicle and fled the scene on NW California Boulevard, leaving the victim with critical head injuries. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested 60-year-old Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. on Oct. 9 on NW California Boulevard just south of its intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. Niemczyk said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash occurred.

Detectives spent two weeks reviewing video, physical evidence and other leads before identifying Aude as a suspect. A geofence warrant that sought cellphone location data from the crash area during the time of the crash showed Aude's phone pinging off nearby cell towers at the time, Niemczyk said, which led investigators to him and to vehicles registered in his name. When detectives examined his vehicle, they found damage to the front bumper and hood consistent with striking a pedestrian, along with presumptive positive results for blood, though further testing is needed. Fasteners from the vehicle's inner fender well recovered at the crash scene matched fasteners missing from Aude's vehicle. cards.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud, Money Laundering Case
cards.teaser: A 22-year-old New York man was arrested near the Canadian border and extradited to St. Lucie County after detectives traced a stolen Port St. Lucie real estate check through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers.
cards.body:
A 22-year-old New York man is facing charges in St. Lucie County after a multi-jurisdictional investigation into an organized check fraud and money laundering scheme, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday. Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx, was arrested after detectives with the Sheriff's Office Economic Crimes Unit traced stolen funds from a Port St. Lucie real estate company back to his personal bank account.

According to the Sheriff's Office, a check mailed by the real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered and deposited into a bank account set up using a stolen identity. Detectives said the stolen funds were then moved through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers in an effort to conceal their origin before ending up in Diallo's personal account. Investigators obtained an arrest warrant charging Diallo with money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more, and grand theft.

On Oct. 14, Canadian border authorities apprehended Diallo as he attempted to enter Canada from the United States. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Bond on the three charges was set at a combined $30,000.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro credited the Economic Crimes Unit for the arrest. “Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice,” Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable.”

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee in 4-3 Vote
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause following a hazing scandal and a no-confidence vote, and named interim Chief Paul Langel to lead the department.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, following months of controversy, hazing allegations, and a no-confidence vote against him. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early.

The board appointed Paul Langel as interim chief. Langel has 30 years of experience in the district and is a familiar face there. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process."

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident. Those disciplined firefighters have called Lee's termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership. One of the terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson, offered a different view of the board's decision. "I think it was a step in the right direction," Hutchinson said. "I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department."

Asked whether the terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out but said he needs time to learn the details of the cases. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen," he said. "I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics."

hero.headline: Leon County probe: CBP agents at polling site tried to vote, not enforce
hero.body:
Leon County election officials and the FBI have concluded that Customs and Border Protection agents seen near an early voting site this week were mistakenly trying to vote before leaving the state, not conducting an immigration enforcement action. A separate incident involving an armed arrest near a Key Largo polling place remains under review by Monroe County election officials. Both episodes drew scrutiny because federal law bars armed officers or troops from operating near polling places, and the Trump administration has repeatedly assured election officials that federal agents would not be stationed at voting sites.

The Leon County incident began Monday when two CBP vehicles parked outside the Northeast Branch Library, described by county election supervisor Mark Earley as the busiest early voting site in the county. The vehicles stayed about 10 minutes before leaving. Earley said his office received no calls from voters about the incident, but he filed a complaint with the FBI because voters may experience intimidation. On Friday, Earley's office said the county sheriff's office and FBI determined the vehicles belonged to a team of agents normally stationed in south Florida who had been reassigned to another state. While driving north to their new post, they stopped at the last Florida polling place on their route after realizing they would not be in the state on Election Day. Earley said the agents mistakenly believed they could vote there, even though they were not Leon County voters, and left immediately once they learned otherwise. He said he accepts that account and considers it an isolated incident consistent with assurances that federal agents would not be stationed at polling sites.

A CBP spokesperson said the officers were traveling in a government vehicle from Florida to Brownsville, Texas, in support of an out-of-state deployment, and that the stop was not an immigration enforcement action. The officers, who were out of uniform, asked whether they could vote early before leaving the state and were told they were only eligible to vote in their home county. The spokesperson said the officers thanked staff and promptly departed, and that government personnel, like all eligible Americans, may exercise their right to vote.

The second incident occurred Tuesday outside the Murray Nelson Government Center in Key Largo, where a community group posted video showing masked and armed federal agents conducting what appeared to be a traffic stop near the polling site. A representative of the group 50501 Key Largo said it was unclear why the agents were there and raised concern that their presence could intimidate voters. Monroe County election supervisor Sherri Hodies said CBP told her agents were trying to pull over a suspect who turned toward the government center, and her office is investigating. A CBP spokesperson said Border Patrol agents assigned to the Marathon Station stopped a vehicle on U.S. Highway 1 as part of a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Arwiin Pillay, described as a Malaysian national in the country illegally with prior charges for drug possession and battery. The spokesperson said the driver pulled into a parking lot adjacent to the polling location, where agents arrested Pillay and left shortly after. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has said agents would only be present at polling places if there were a threat to the site or if they were serving a warrant on someone they were actively tracking.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police: Two Vehicles May Have Hit Man in Fatal Crash
cards.teaser: Investigators now believe a 63-year-old man found unconscious near Northwest University Boulevard was struck by two separate vehicles, and police have released new images seeking help identifying both drivers.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police have updated their investigation into an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie man seriously injured, now saying two vehicles may have struck him rather than one. Detectives believe the victim was hit near the intersection of Northwest University Boulevard and Northwest California Boulevard by one vehicle traveling northbound and another traveling southbound.

The crash happened at approximately 12:56 a.m., when the man was found unconscious in the roadway suffering from severe head injuries. In an earlier update, police said surveillance video from a nearby business captured the incident and showed what investigators believed was a white four-door sedan striking the man before fleeing the scene without stopping.

As detectives continued reviewing evidence and surveillance footage, they developed information indicating a second vehicle may also have been involved in the crash. Police are now working to identify both vehicles and their drivers and have released images of the vehicles to the public.

Anyone who recognizes either vehicle, was in the area at the time of the crash, witnessed the incident, or has dashcam or surveillance video from the area is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Lee, Names Langel Interim Chief
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 on Thursday to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, ending months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against him. The board appointed Paul Langel, who has 30 years of experience in the district, as interim chief.

The vote comes two months after five firefighters were displaced for allegedly turning a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and using it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident. Those disciplined firefighters have called their termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

Langel said he sees his new role as a chance to move the department forward after a turbulent stretch. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the terminated firefighters could eventually get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics," he said.

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the firefighters terminated over the hazing allegations, said he welcomed the board's decision to remove Lee. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," he said. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early. The board's action marks a significant shift in a controversy that has consumed the fire district for months, and it now falls to Langel to steer the department through its next chapter.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man Killed in Thursday Crash With Semi-Truck in Indian River County
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday morning after his SUV collided with a semi-truck at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in unincorporated Indian River County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 6:45 a.m.

FHP said a Freightliner semi-truck was stopped at a stop sign on westbound 49th Street and attempting to turn left onto 66th Avenue. At the same time, a Dodge Durango was traveling north in the inside lane of 66th Avenue, which had no traffic controls at that intersection. Troopers said the Freightliner entered the path of the SUV, and the front of the Durango struck the left side of the semi-trailer. Both vehicles came to rest in the area of the collision.

The driver of the SUV, the 60-year-old Vero Beach man, was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne. He was pronounced dead just after 8 a.m., according to FHP. The driver of the Freightliner, a 59-year-old Jacksonville man, was not injured in the crash.

The crash remains under investigation by the Florida Highway Patrol.

cards.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud Scheme
cards.teaser: A 22-year-old New York man was arrested near the Canadian border and extradited to St. Lucie County on charges connected to a stolen, altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company.
cards.body:
A 22-year-old man from New York is facing money laundering and fraud charges after detectives say he helped funnel stolen money from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through a chain of bank accounts, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday. Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx, was extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. following a multi-jurisdictional investigation by the sheriff's office Economic Crimes Unit.

Investigators said a check mailed by the Port St. Lucie real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered and deposited into a bank account opened using a stolen identity. Detectives traced the money through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers that were allegedly used to hide where it came from before it landed in Diallo's personal bank account.

Detectives obtained a warrant charging Diallo with money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more, and grand theft. On Oct. 14, Canadian border authorities apprehended Diallo as he attempted to cross from the United States into Canada. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County. Bond was set at a total of $30,000 for the three charges.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro credited the Economic Crimes Unit for tracking down the suspect. "Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice," Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable."

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Newspaper Driver in Oct. 9 Hit-and-Run
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a newspaper delivery driver in connection with an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie man in critical condition. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested Eric Saint Aude, 60, on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. Niemczyk said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened. Aude is being held on $45,000 bond.

The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. He had no identification or cellphone with him, but investigators used data from a Garmin exercise watch he was wearing to trace his route back to his house and identify him. Niemczyk said the victim often exercised at night when the weather was cooler and was known to walk on the road and medians. The chief said the victim has significant head trauma and is unable to speak, and while he is expected to survive, his quality of life may not be the same as it was before the crash.

Detectives reviewed video, physical evidence and other leads in the two weeks following the crash. Niemczyk said a geofence warrant seeking cellphone location data from the crash area and time produced a lead showing Aude's phone had pinged off cell towers there at the time of the crash, pointing investigators toward Aude and vehicles registered to him. Detectives then located and examined his vehicle, finding damage to the front bumper and hood consistent with striking a pedestrian, along with presumptive positive results for blood. Further testing is needed to confirm those results. Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle's inner fender-well fasteners at the scene and found that several matching fasteners were missing from Aude's vehicle.

Investigators are still searching for a second vehicle that was traveling southbound near the crash scene. Niemczyk said distant video showed a vehicle traveling in each direction, but it was difficult to determine what happened. Police are trying to learn whether the second vehicle also struck the victim or whether its driver witnessed the crash. "We're very confident that the vehicle that we have and the person that we've arrested are responsible for the majority of what occurred,

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Water Tank Mural Named National Tank of the Year
cards.teaser: The painted water storage tank at Jaycee Park in Fort Pierce has won Tnemec Company's 2026 Tank of the Year contest, beating out 11 other finalists nationwide. Artist Christian Stanley and Fort Pierce Utilities Authority celebrated the honor.
cards.body:
A water storage tank at Jaycee Park in Fort Pierce has been named the winner of the 2026 Tank of the Year contest, an annual competition run by Tnemec Company, Inc., a maker of high-performance coatings. The company announced the winner and its Top 12 finalists on Friday, selecting the Fort Pierce tank over entries from across the country, including Detroit Lakes, Minnesota, which won the separate People's Choice award.

The tank features a mural by Christian Stanley of C. Stanley Creative showing sea turtles, dolphins, manatees, pelicans and tropical fish, turning the ground storage tank into a tribute to Florida's coastal environment and wildlife. The structure is coated with Tnemec's Series 1026 Enduratone product. Tnemec said a panel of water tank enthusiasts judged entries on artistic value, significance to the community and the challenges involved in completing each project.

Stanley, who grew up in Stuart, said he learned of the win from his sales representative. "Pretty excited," Stanley said. "I got the call earlier from our sales rep. He was excited to share that we were the first-place winner of Tnemec's Tank of the Year. And yeah, we're just beyond excited, and I'm excited to share that with them and with the community that they have an award-winning piece of public art there in their community." Stanley and his wife, Jessica, traveled from Central Florida to apply a UV clear coat to the tank. He said the project carries extra meaning because of his ties to the area. "We were runners-up in 2024, and that was exciting," he said. "But I was like, man, I really want to try. And I know we can make something that would win the first-place award. So, it's, you know, taken a couple of years for us to get there. But I'm excited that we were able to come some bring something together and that Fort Pierce trusted us to make something that we felt was going to be really impactful and iconic for the community there." He added, "I grew up in Stuart, so it was great to visit kind of my old hometown and just be back in the community and be a part of it again, and to kind of leave a footprint. This thing will kind of continue to have a life of its own beyond just the just the tank. And it'll have a bigger footprint than even what we could anticipate. So, it's really cool to get some recognition for the for the award. And we're excited to see what comes next from this."

Fort Pierce Utilities Authority credited its collaboration with Stanley and the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency this summer for transforming the tank into a local landmark. "We are thrilled and deeply grateful to receive the Tank of the Year award," the utility said in a statement attributed to Rachel Tennant, FPUA Director of Public Affairs Sustainability. "Thank you to everyone who voted and supported us, and to the teams who made it happen. It has been an absolute pleasure and honor for our team here at FPUA to collaborate with the artist and the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency this summer, turning the Jaycee Park Water Tank into a Fort Pierce landmark." Kevin Morris, Tnemec's director of sales for the water tank market, said the contest has run for 20 years and praised this year's entries. "Fort Pierce is a great example of how a water tank can become more than a functional structure," Morris said. "It can become a landmark that residents are proud to call their own." The Fort Pierce tank will appear as the January image in Tnemec's 2027 water tank calendar, alongside the other finalists and nominees from the contest.

hero.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud, Money Laundering Case
hero.teaser: A 22-year-old New York man was extradited to St. Lucie County after detectives traced a stolen, altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through multiple bank accounts. He faces money laundering, scheme to defraud and grand theft charges with bond set at $30,000.
hero.body:
A 22-year-old man from New York is facing money laundering and fraud charges after the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said he took part in a scheme that targeted a Port St. Lucie real estate company. The sheriff's office said its Economic Crimes Unit conducted a multi-jurisdictional investigation that led to the arrest of Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx.

According to the sheriff's office, a check mailed by the real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered and deposited into a bank account that had been set up using a stolen identity. Detectives said they traced the stolen funds through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers allegedly used to hide where the money came from before it was ultimately deposited into Diallo's personal bank account.

Detectives obtained an arrest warrant charging Diallo with money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud $50,000 or more, and grand theft. On Oct. 14, Canadian border authorities apprehended Diallo as he attempted to enter Canada from the United States. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Bond was set at $30,000 total for the three charges.

"Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice," Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable."

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee Without Cause
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee after months of hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote, naming 30-year veteran Paul Langel as interim chief.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against him. The board named Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief following the vote.

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appeared to show the alleged hazing, and three of the firefighters involved ultimately lost their jobs. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early.

Langel addressed his new role after the board's vote. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the firefighters terminated over the bug-zapper incident could get their jobs back, Langel said, "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics."

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the firefighters terminated in connection with the hazing scandal, said he saw the board's decision on Lee as a positive step for the department. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," he said. The disciplined firefighters have called the termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee, Names Interim Replacement
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Chief Jeff Lee without cause after a hazing scandal and a no-confidence vote. Board members appointed longtime district veteran Paul Langel as interim chief.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against his leadership. The board immediately appointed Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief.

The vote comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three of the firefighters ultimately lost their jobs. Those disciplined firefighters have called their terminations retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

Langel addressed his new role after the vote. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the terminated firefighters could regain their positions, Langel said, "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics."

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the firefighters terminated in the hazing case, said he viewed Lee's firing as a positive step for the department. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," Hutchinson said. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation under his contract, which ends ahead of schedule. Questions remain about the terminated firefighters' employment status as Langel settles into his interim role.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Partners with Treasure Coast Food Bank for Food Drive
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County is teaming up with the Treasure Coast Food Bank for a county-wide food drive, with county facilities serving as drop-off sites for shelf-stable donations ahead of the holidays.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Board of County Commissioners is partnering with the Treasure Coast Food Bank for a county-wide food drive in October. County facilities will serve as donation drop-off sites for residents who want to give shelf-stable food items.

The Treasure Coast Food Bank has identified its most-needed items for the drive. Those include canned vegetables and fruit, soups and stews, rice and grains, pasta and pasta sauce, tuna, peanut butter and jelly, cereal, and snacks such as granola bars, crackers and nuts.

Residents can drop off donations at designated St. Lucie County facilities taking part in the drive. The county is encouraging anyone who can contribute shelf-stable goods to bring them to one of the participating sites during the drive.

County officials said donations collected through the drive will go toward supporting families in need across St. Lucie County through the Treasure Coast Food Bank's distribution network.

hero.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud Case After Border Arrest
hero.body:
A 20-year-old Bronx, New York, man has been extradited to St. Lucie County after Canadian border authorities arrested him as he tried to enter Canada, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said. Gibrill Diallo faces charges of money laundering, a scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more and grand theft in connection with a stolen check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company.

The Sheriff's Office said the check was altered and deposited into a bank account opened using a stolen identity. Detectives traced the funds through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers before they were deposited into Diallo's personal bank account.

Diallo was arrested Oct. 21 and held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before his extradition. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said detectives followed the money and pursued leads across jurisdictions to build the case.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee, Taxpayers Face $350,000 Severance
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire Board voted Wednesday to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee's contract without cause, ending his tenure with a severance package expected to total about $350,000. The firing follows a no-confidence vote among union firefighters, in which more than 74% of those who participated said they had no confidence in Lee.

The vote capped months of fallout from a hazing investigation into videos involving firefighters at Station 1A. Some videos showed a modified bug zapper being used to shock three apprentice firefighters while on duty in 2024. Others showed water being dumped on two firefighters and a dead raccoon placed inside a fire vehicle. A third-party investigator concluded the videos depicted hazing, and veteran firefighters Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Chris Baldwin were fired as a result, though all three disputed that characterization and said the incidents were consensual pranks. "It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun," Hutchinson said. "We're all still friends," Boudrias added. Their firings drew outcry from firefighters, former firefighters and community members, many of whom packed the Fire Administration building Wednesday holding signs or wearing shirts in support of the three men. "Not only have they lost their jobs, but they also lost their reputations," one public commentator said.

St. Lucie County Commissioner and Fire Board member Jamie Fowler said the decision to remove Lee was not about a single misstep. "At the end of the day, it's gotten very messy. It's not about one single decision that he's made. It's about bringing peace and calm and respect back to the district and the men and women that serve this community every day, and it just got to a point where he was not effective anymore," Fowler said. Fire Board member and business owner Travis Leonard made the motion to fire Lee, pointing to a letter Lee had sent the board days earlier suggesting it may be time for a "mutually agreeable retirement and leadership transition" because "the position of fire chief requires confidence." "Coming from the private sector, anytime an employee gives their notice, I terminate them; I found they've checked out," Leonard said. St. Lucie County Commissioner and Fire Board member James Clasby said the vote reflected what the union's no-confidence poll had already shown. "There was a large desire to have a change in leadership, and we delivered that today," Clasby said.

After terminating Lee's contract, the board appointed Deputy Chief Paul Langel as interim fire chief. The district also plans to hire a recruiter to search for Lee's permanent replacement. "I am excited to move this district forward, to begin the healing process of the issues that we've been dealing with, as of recent, and to instill trust," Langel said.

The leadership shakeup comes as the firefighters union continues negotiating with the district to reinstate Boudrias, Hutchinson and Baldwin. Union Representative Ryan Sapp called Lee's termination a "positive step forward." "I think moving forward, the ultimate goal here is to just move forward and get things back to a level field and continue providing the services to our community," Sapp said. "The biggest thing today is we worked together and came together as a local, glad to see my membership stepped up and let their voices be heard." The union vote also showed about 92% of firefighters had no confidence in Assistant Chief Brian Gonzalez and 97% had no confidence in District Attorney Kim Sabol, who has submitted her notice of retirement amid the controversy. The Fire Board is now searching for her replacement as well.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Suspect in Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured 63-Year-Old
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police announced Friday the arrest of a suspect in a hit-and-run crash that critically injured a 63-year-old resident earlier this month. The crash happened about 12:56 a.m. on Oct. 9 near NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries and taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where the victim remained in critical condition, police said.

Detectives reviewed surveillance video and gathered additional evidence as they worked to identify the vehicle or vehicles involved and those who left the scene. As of Thursday, investigators believed they were looking for two vehicles.

Police planned to release more information at a news conference scheduled for 1 p.m. Friday at department headquarters.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee Without Cause
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Chief Jeff Lee after months of hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote. Interim Chief Paul Langel says his job now is to begin healing the department.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against him. The board immediately appointed Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief.

"I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process."

The board's decision comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three of the firefighters were ultimately terminated. Jordon Hutchinson, one of the fired firefighters, called the board's vote on Lee a step in the right direction. "I don't think today was about us by any means," Hutchinson said. "I think it was the best thing for the entire department." The disciplined firefighters have said their terminations were retaliation for complaints they had previously filed against district leadership.

Asked whether the terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel said he was not ready to make that call. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen," he said. "I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics." Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man, 60, Dies in Crash at 66th Avenue and 49th Street
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. The Florida Highway Patrol said a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was turning left from a stop sign on westbound 49th Street when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. His next of kin had not been notified, according to the crash report.

The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner reported no injuries.

hero.headline: 86-Year-Old Found Dead After Car Plunges Into Indian River Lagoon in Vero Beach
hero.body:
An 86-year-old man was found dead inside a car pulled from the Indian River Lagoon in Vero Beach after witnesses said the vehicle drove through a fence at a condo complex and into the water. Police have not yet identified the man. Authorities said he had gone missing the night before the car was discovered.

Residents at the condo complex said they knew the driver. Tire marks were visible near the scene where the car breached the fence before entering the lagoon. Police worked for hours to pull the silver Honda CR-V from the water as the investigation got underway.

The crash left a visible mark on the community. Residents on Greytwig Road were later seen cleaning up the parking lot, removing mud and scrubbing away tire marks left behind. Several described the scene as unsettling.

Police have not released the identity of the victim and continue to investigate what led up to the crash. The case remains active as authorities work to determine the circumstances that caused the vehicle to leave the roadway and enter the lagoon.

The board appointed Paul Langel as interim chief following Lee's termination. Langel is a familiar face within the district, bringing 30 years of experience to the role. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process." Asked about the possibility that the terminated firefighters could regain their jobs, Langel said, "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics."

cards.headline: Red Flag Warning Keeps St. Lucie Beaches Under High Hazard Advisory
cards.teaser: Four to six foot surf and rip current risk prompted St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue to urge swimmers toward lifeguarded beaches like Pepper Park and Waveland Beach.
cards.body:
A red flag warning has put St. Lucie County beaches under a high hazard advisory, with waves between four and six feet crashing along the shoreline at Fort Pierce Inlet State Park on Wednesday. The dangerous surf and rip current risk prompted St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue to urge swimmers to head to lifeguarded beaches such as Pepper Park and Waveland Beach, where officials say red or double red flags will likely keep flying for the next few days.

Fort Pierce Inlet State Park was among several St. Lucie County beaches under the red flag warning, which officials tied to a low pressure system off the eastern United States coast in the mid-Atlantic. Fort Pierce resident Lee Bertucelli described the water conditions bluntly. "The sea was angry today my friends," he said.

The rough surf made for challenging conditions for people in the water. "It was very windy and very choppy and it's really challenging because you have to negotiate all of the chop," foil surfer Lisa Rose said. Surfer Jodi Riley said she only ventured in to her waist rather than bringing her surfboard. "I went in, not with my surfboard, but like, to my waist and it's just, it's rough and it's just not super safe for like, I'm sort of a beginner so not safe for me, but like, some of the other surfers have definitely been out," Riley said.

Bertucelli said he stayed cautious despite enjoying the waves. "I went in, you know, not too far. The waves were fun, but again not too far, didn't want to deal with rip tides or anything else," he said. St. Lucie County officials say rip currents are possible under these conditions and advise swimmers caught in one not to panic and to swim parallel to the shoreline. Ocean Rescue continues to stress that lifeguarded beaches like Pepper Park and Waveland Beach are the safest option while the red flag advisory remains in effect.

hero.headline: Veterans Golf Free as Tee It Up for the Troops Debuts at Lost Lake in Hobe Sound
hero.body:
A Veterans Day golf tournament is bringing paying players together with local veterans, who will golf for free, when Tee It Up for the Troops holds its event for the first time at The Club at Lost Lake in Hobe Sound on Wednesday, Nov. 11. The field is capped at 106 golfers, with registration priced at $750 per player, and veterans paired into foursomes will not pay to play.

Chris LaRocque, president and executive director of Tee It Up for the Troops, said the cause is personal. "It's very close to my heart," LaRocque said in an ARC Florida interview. "I'm an Army Reserve major myself." He said the nonprofit has deployed more than $20 million and supported more than 400,000 veterans through programs that help with the transition to civilian jobs and provide support for post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injuries.

Proceeds from the Hobe Sound tournament will also support local veterans programs, including PGA HOPE in South Florida, LaRocque said. PGA HOPE introduces veterans and active-duty service members to golf as a way to support their physical, mental, social and emotional well-being.

The tournament will take place at The Club at Lost Lake, 8300 SE Fazio Drive in Hobe Sound. Registration and event information are available through Tee It Up for the Troops.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee Without Cause
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 on Thursday to terminate Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against him. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early.

The board also voted to appoint Paul Langel as interim chief. Langel has 30 years of experience in the district and is a familiar face to its firefighters. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process."

The board's decision comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three of the firefighters ultimately lost their jobs. Those firefighters have called their termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership. Jordon Hutchinson, one of the terminated firefighters, said of Lee's removal, "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department."

Asked whether the three terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen," he said. "I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics." Langel's comments leave open the question of reinstatement as he begins transitioning into the interim chief role.

hero.body:

The Florida Highway Patrol said a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was turning left from a stop sign on westbound 49th Street when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. His next of kin had not been notified, according to the crash report.

hero.headline: Martin County Commission Approves School Zone for Citrus Grove Elementary
hero.body:
Martin County commissioners have unanimously approved a new school zone on Southwest Newfield Parkway outside Citrus Grove Elementary School, answering years of safety concerns from parents who say the current 45 mph speed limit puts children at risk. Many families who live in the Canopy Creek community across the street from the school walk their children to class each morning and afternoon, crossing the busy roadway.

Kelly Ribaudo, the school's PTA president and Martin County PTA Advocacy Chair, said she has spent the last five years asking the county to install a school zone. "We've had so many near misses with the kids just from people not paying attention," Ribaudo said. "Everyone has a right to a free and public education and they should be safe getting there. Our main priority should be the kids not the traffic." Parent Kendall George said the current traffic conditions frighten her. "It scares me," George said. "These cars are driving 45 miles an hour plus."

At a previous Martin County Commission meeting, commissioners sided with the parents. "Whatever the number is there is no price to someone getting hurt," Commissioner Edward Ciampi said. "You will absolutely get a school zone." School Principal Rose Rynca said the need has grown as new communities bring more students to the area. "The amount of students crossing Newfield Parkway has definitely increased," Rynca said. "This speed zone is going to really really improve the safety of students." George said a school zone sign will help alert drivers. "It's letting drivers know that, hey there's a school here, there's children crossing, and we have to slow down," George said.

A timeline for when the school zone will actually go in on Southwest Newfield Parkway has not been pinned down by the county. Until then, Ribaudo is urging drivers to use caution near the school regardless of posted signage. "Slow down if you see a school, even if there's not a school zone sign, slow down," Ribaudo said. With the school zone approved, parents say their next priority is pushing the county for better street lighting along the corridor.

A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after a semi-truck turned into the path of his SUV in unincorporated Indian River County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 6:45 a.m. at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street.

Troopers said a Freightliner semi-truck was attempting a left turn from a stop sign at westbound 49th Street onto 66th Avenue when it entered the path of a northbound Dodge Durango traveling in the inside lane. The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead just after 8 a.m. The Freightliner's driver, a 59-year-old Jacksonville man, was not injured. The crash remains under investigation by FHP.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire Chief Jeff Lee Terminated; Deputy Chief Langel Named Interim
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District board voted Wednesday to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, ending his tenure after months of turmoil over a hazing investigation and mounting criticism of district leadership. Lee did not attend the heated meeting where commissioners made the decision.

In a statement issued Thursday to a reporter, Lee pointed to improvements he said he delivered during his time leading the district. The Fire District itself noted in an October 9 statement that from 2023 to 2026 the district saw approximately 19% average pay-plan growth, an increase of about 100 uniformed personnel, and improved minimum engine staffing from two to three firefighters. The district also said it expanded employee benefits, increased retirement-health contributions, and invested in additional training, equipment and facilities. "That's really all I have to say," Lee told the reporter.

Lee's exit follows fallout from videos showing probationary firefighters being shocked with a modified bug zapper, conduct a third-party investigator concluded amounted to hazing. Three veteran firefighters were fired after that investigation, sparking backlash from firefighters, their families and community members who said the punishment was too harsh. "Not only have they lost their jobs, but they lost their reputation," one speaker told the board Wednesday. Lee's departure also came after the firefighters union delivered an overwhelming vote of no confidence in district leadership, though board member and St. Lucie County Commissioner Jamie Fowler said that vote was not the sole reason for his removal. "At the end of the day, it's gotten very messy," Fowler said. "It's not about one single decision that he's made. It's about bringing peace and calm and respect." Lee had previously signaled in a letter to the board that his time as chief could be ending, writing that the position "requires confidence" and raising the possibility of a mutually agreeable retirement.

Deputy Chief Paul Langel has been appointed interim fire chief while the district searches for a permanent replacement. "Personally, I don't think there is a culture problem," Langel said, adding he plans to visit fire stations and talk with employees individually and in groups to assess morale before deciding on next steps. Commissioners plan to hire a headhunter to search for a permanent chief both inside and outside the district, according to Fowler. The district and firefighters union are expected to keep discussing possible reinstatement of the three fired firefighters, with union representative Ryan Sapp saying he is eager to see the sides "come back together." The board is also working with an outside law firm to overhaul complaint policies after a September 30 meeting identified what members called "a significant gap" in existing procedures. Commissioner James Clasby said Lee's contract terms could leave taxpayers responsible for more than $350,000 in severance, and he wants the next chief's contract written to avoid similar terms. "That's the consequences of firing somebody with those terms," Clasby said.
